subindicator: spontaneous solution of a novel problem despite social cues and relevant experience
task_context: zoo-based novel-problem task with social cues and prior relevant experience
interpretation: Sloth bears failed to spontaneously solve the novel problem even with social cues and relevant experience. This coexists with positive spatial-transposition evidence, so it narrows A rather than setting A=0.

task_context: familiarity/individual-recognition experiments in threespine and ninespine sticklebacks
interpretation: No evidence for individual recognition. This does not erase other communication/social-learning capacities; it narrows social-recognition subcomponents.

subindicator: directed social learning of a novel technical solution
interpretation: Social-learning opportunity did not increase problem-solving success, although observers tended to show reduced neophobia and lower-ranking individuals attended more to demonstrators. This is a boundary on solution copying, not absence of all social influence.
